The painter's eye is drawn to the crowded middle, where many short lists overlap and look urgent. The weigher points the other way: the long edge clue is the most settled, because the longer a run is the fewer places it can hide, and it anchors the whole board from the rim inward. Disciplined hands start at the edge, and the middles submit to them.
